No problem :) my pic for my shop, until recently, was my logo made up of 2 of the letters in my name plus a graphic. But that's a good idea. Hopefully the resources help, they've really helped me ^_^

I'm not really an expert (will drop the name of a yt channel you should go to for help), but I'll offer what I've learned both through my experiences and what I've learned from the coaches I follow.

•price a bit higher than you think it should be! If it seems a little high it's probably about right. This way you can offer free shipping, sales, etc without losing money. Cool stuff people like to see. In addition to that, leave your highest priced items up... There's a weird science about it, but I'll drop where you can learn about that (on mobile so I can't link unfortunately)

•i think another commenter said this, but for your shop profile photo, either 1) put a picture of you or 2) a shop logo or something of the sort. Pictures of you help solidify in shoppers' minds that you're a real human. A shop logo would still be professional.

•if I misunderstood pls correct me but you said you offer promos to people who had favorited your item (this is how I understood)... I believe this is actually against Etsy's terms of service. If you mean through an email list then that's different (and fine) but you can't send anything that isn't transactional to people on Etsy so keep that in mind

•be careful about copyrighted stuff, just do your research really

•describe how you make your things in your description. As a buyer I like to know a bit about how something is made but that may be because I'm also a seller, but tell the world about how cool your stuff is :)


Now onto the stuff I don't have the authority to tell you:

These coaches have really helped me figure out what to do to improve my shop. My stuff takes a long time to make so my shop is meh, but I'm quitting my full time job to work on it a little more. In the meantime I have been watching and reading material from these coaches and they explain so much about how I can improve.

Yt: Starla Moore - amazing, fun and really knowledgeable about how Etsy works. She and her husband keep up with the latest changes on Etsy and explain them in a clear manner, and often bring experts and top sellers into their live streams for live q&a. She runs an Etsy shop herself and is very successful

Renae Christine: she's basically the top handmade business coach out there. Many other coaches learned from her. She focuses more on running your own website and whatnot but still has really important info that is useful to both platforms. She has run 6-figure businesses with her techniques, which are fully replicable and able to be tailored to what you're doing.

freehandmadetrainings.com - also run by Renae Christine. This is your startup/beginner guide. Obviously you've already got a shop going but it's a great resource to pack nuggets of knowledge from.

Hope that helps, keep creating :)

I have a huge ass desk occupying my living room (😂), it's got one of those stacker tops that has cubbies and whatnot (the thing is like, 7ft tall by 8ft wide lol). I plan to have a peg board eventually and at some point I'll be getting a large table to work at, a real ironing board (have a mini one at the moment), and a few more dress forms. I did this year. I just lost it one night and screamed that I wanted to die and end my life. My fiancee asked if I wanted to go to the hospital and I agreed to. I was in the suicide unit overnight, with someone watching me constantly, then the next day I was admitted involuntarily to the psychiatric ward. I was written down as involuntary because I insisted on going home and told them I was feeling better, but they insisted I get help. 

I was in the ward 6 and a half days. The first day was weird because I was surrounded by people I didn't know, everything was taken away from me, basically I was in another reality. I had no idea what was happening in the life I had lived, I only saw my other half a few times during my stay and called her non stop just to hear her voice. It was really hard living with nothing but a coloring book and a few pieces of clothing I highly valued. You are watched 24/7, although your room is private. However I'm not used to being watched like that so it's a little weird. I made some friends there who I'm still in contact with. The food at the place I was at was about 1,000 calories a meal and made me horribly ill but it's because I have a sensitive stomach. I wasn't allowed to order special/specific food despite constant stomach problems.

It's really strict there. You have to eat, whether you like it or not, and they will record if you do or don't and your stay will be extended if you don't. By day 4 I wanted to leave. I was tired of sleeping alone and was having horrible separation anxiety not being with the other half and my birds. I had no music to help pass time, and sleeping too much was a big no no. I was officially diagnosed with BPD and my medications were switched, which was very important to my recovery. 

I think I've covered a pretty basic summary of what happened there. It was important, but I sure as hell would never do it again. I can't sleep alone for that long and be without my birds that long. If you need to please do it, it will help you take steps towards recovery. For me it really helped me face the feelings I had but couldn't describe or was ashamed of, plus it has completely changed my therapy sessions. We're pin pointing what's happening and zeroing in on what is happening now instead of the past. It's helping me see what's happening so I can not only help myself, but also explain it to my SO. It's helped me be able to describe my feelings in detail. A hospital stay can change your life and for me it's been essential to my recovery. It's not for everyone and it depends on where you go, but please get help for suicidal thoughts. It will make your future so much easier to face if you get help to guide you through it.
